candidates.definition: A T cell population characterized by not expressing the CD8 molecule on its surface.

candidates.label: effector T cell function
candidates.definition: The function inhering in a T cell that is realized in an immune response that results from the T cell receptor binding to the MHC:epitope complex.

candidates.label: cultured effector T cell population
candidates.definition: A cell culture including cells that have an effector T cell function

candidates.label: epitope specific T cell proliferation
candidates.definition: A biological process where T cells proliferate resulting from the recognition of a T cell epitope.

candidates.label: time step
candidates.definition: A time step is a one-dimensional temporal region that has a start time and an ending time and thus a finite duration.

candidates.label: time stamp
candidates.definition: A time stamp is a data descriptor that is used to describe either a temporal region or a data item that is related to a temporal region, e.g. a time stamped measurement datum. If the time stamp refers to a time step/one-dimensional temporal region, the indication of a time stamp alignment is required

candidates.label: t-statistic
candidates.definition: A t-statistic is a ratio of the departure of an estimated parameter from its notional value and its standard error.

candidates.label: T associations
candidates.definition: A stellar association containing many T Tauri stars. Examples include the Taurus-Auriga T association, the nearby TW Hydrae association, and Vela T1 and T2.

candidates.label: T dwarfs
candidates.definition: A type of brown dwarf with an effective temperature between about 1200 K and 500 K, i.e. colder than the preceding type L dwarf. The spectra of T dwarfs are characterized by the presence of methane bands in the near infrared. The presence of these bands, broad H_{2}O features, and H_2 collision-induced absorption radically alter the spectral energy distributions of T dwarfs compared to a black body at the same temperature. Hence near-infrared colors become increasingly blue (J - K ~ 0) as compared to L dwarfs. The first T dwarf, called Gl 229B, was discovered by Nakajima et al. The spectral classification scheme (subtypes T0 to T9) currently used was defined by Burgasser et al.

candidates.label: T Tauri stars
candidates.definition: A member of a class of young stellar objects of roughly 1 solar mass showing strong infrared excess emission attributed to circumstellar disks and found within or close to molecular clouds. T Tauri stars are protostars in the final stages of formation to become a stable main sequence star. The nuclear reactions in their core have not yet stabilized and the stars are known for the variability of their brightness.

candidates.label: Classical T Tauri stars
candidates.definition: A T Tauri star in which accretion from a circumstellar disk is responsible for ultraviolet and infrared excess emission and for a moderate to strong emission line spectrum superimposed on the photospheric spectrum. Classical T Tauri stars probably evolve into weak-line T Tauri stars when their disks are fully accreted by the stars.

candidates.label: evaporative light scattering detector
candidates.definition: An evaporative light scattering detector is a detector that detects material by way of the measurement of the scattering of light after nebulization with an inert carrier gas and evaporation of the solvent. [Allotrope]

candidates.label: evaporative light scattering detection
candidates.definition: A detection method where a liquid containing the sample is atomized in a gas, forming small droplets which are allowed to evaporate leaving the sample as fine particles. The suspended particles pass through a light beam and the scattered light transmitted by the particles is sensed by a photodiode or photomultiplier tube. The response can be quantitative and relative to the amount of molecules eluting. [Allotrope, CHMO]

candidates.label: DynamicLightScattering
candidates.definition: Dynamic light scattering (DLS) is a technique in physics that can be used to determine the size distribution profile of small particles in suspension or polymers in solution. In the scope of DLS, temporal fluctuations are usually analyzed using the intensity or photon auto-correlation function (also known as photon correlation spectroscopy - PCS or quasi-elastic light scattering - QELS).

candidates.label: LightScattering
candidates.definition: Light scattering is the way light behaves when it interacts with a medium that contains particles or the boundary between different mediums where defects or structures are present. It is different than the effects of refraction, where light undergoes a change in index of refraction as it passes from one medium to another, or reflection, where light reflects back into the same medium, both of which are governed by Snell’s law. Light scattering can be caused by factors such as the nature, texture, or specific structures of a surface and the presence of gas, liquid, or solid particles through which light propagates, as well as the nature of the light itself, of its wavelengths and polarization states. It usually results in diffuse light and can also affect the dispersion of color.

candidates.label: light scattering
candidates.definition: A scattering method for determining structure by measuring the change in direction or energy of scattered visible light. Light is scattered by the electrons surrounding the atomic nuclei in the sample.

candidates.label: dynamic light scattering
candidates.definition: A light scattering for determining the size distribution of a sample of small particles in solution by illuminating the sample with a light source (usually a laser) and measuring the time-dependent fluctuations in the intensity of the scattered light caused by Brownian motion.

candidates.label: multi-angle light scattering
candidates.definition: A method for determining structure by measuring the change in direction or energy of scattered visible light at a number of different angles, none of which are close to the angle of incidence of the light.

candidates.label: Rayleigh scattering spectroscopy
candidates.definition: A method for determining structure by measuring the change in direction or energy of Rayleigh scattered visible light.

candidates.label: hyper Rayleigh scattering spectroscopy
candidates.definition: A method for determining the structure of a liquid sample by measuring the change in direction or energy of hyper-Rayleigh scattered visible light (scattering where photons from the incident laser–-with frequency –-are scattered into photons of the second harmonic–-photons with frequency 2).

candidates.label: near-resonance Rayleigh scattering spectroscopy
candidates.definition: A method for determining structure by measuring the change in direction or energy of Rayleigh scattered visible light, where the wavelength of the incident light corresponds to an energy which is near to an absorption band in the scattering molecules.

candidates.label: resonance Rayleigh scattering spectroscopy
candidates.definition: A method for determining structure by measuring the change in direction or energy of Rayleigh scattered visible light, where the wavelength of the incident light corresponds to an absorption band in the scattering molecules.

candidates.label: forced Rayleigh scattering spectroscopy
candidates.definition: A method for determining structure where a grating created by the interference of two laser beams is written into a sample and a further laser beam is Rayleigh scattered by the grating. The change in direction or energy of the light and the temporal evolution of the scattered beam are measured.

candidates.label: small-angle light scattering
candidates.definition: A method for determining structure by measuring the change in direction or energy of visible light scattered at a small angle (0.1–10°) to the incident light.

candidates.label: static light scattering
candidates.definition: A light scattering for determining structure by measuring the total or time-averaged scattering intensity of scattered visible light as a function of angle.

candidates.label: laser light scattering
candidates.definition: A method for determining structure by measuring the change in direction or energy of scattered visible light. Light (from a laser source) is scattered by the electrons surrounding the atomic nuclei in the sample.

candidates.label: evaporative light scattering detection
candidates.definition: A detection method where a liquid containing the sample is atomised in a gas, forming small droplets which are allowed to evaporate leaving the sample as fine particles. The suspended particles pass through a light beam and the scattered light transmitted by the particles is sensed by a photomultiplier. The response is proportional to the mass of the molecules in the sample.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-evaporative light scattering detection
candidates.definition: A liquid chromatography method where the mobile phase is atomised in a gas, forming small droplets which are allowed to evaporate leaving the sample as fine particles. The suspended particles pass through a light beam and the scattered light transmitted by the particles is sensed by a photomultiplier. The response is proportional to the mass of the molecules in the sample.

candidates.label: electrophoretic light scattering
candidates.definition: A method for determining the electrophoretic mobility and zeta-potential of a sample of colloidal particles in solution by illuminating the sample with a light source (usually a laser) and measuring the time dependent fluctuations in the frequency of the scattered light caused by an oscillating electric field.

candidates.label: dynamic light scattering
candidates.definition: In dynamic light scattering, particle diffusion in solution gives rise to fluctuations in the intensity of the scattered light on the microsecond scale. The hydrodynamic radius of the particles can be easily calculated.

candidates.label: light scattering
candidates.definition: Dynamic and static laser light scattering probes the size, shape, and structure of biological macromolecules or of their assemblies. A beam is focused on an optically clear cylindrical cell containing the sample. Most of the light passes directly through the sample. A small portion of the light is scattered; the scattered light intensity containing information about the scattering particle is detected at an angle (typically in the range 15-180degrees) from the direction of the incident beam.

candidates.label: Light Scattering
candidates.definition: Dispersal of a beam of light into a range of directions as a result of physical interactions.

candidates.label: evaporative light scattering detector
candidates.definition: The evaporative light scattering detector, as its name implies, utilizes a spray that continuously atomizes the column eluent into small droplets. These droplets are allowed to evaporate, leaving the solutes as fine particulate matter suspended in the atomizing gas.

candidates.label: light scattering
candidates.definition: The redirection of a light beam due to interactions with molecules (Rayleigh and Raman scattering) and aerosols (Mie scattering).

candidates.label: elastic light scattering
candidates.definition: Radiation may be scattered by its transmission through a medium containing particles. If the scatter results in no significant change in the wavelength relative to the primary radiation it is called elastic scattering. In cases where the scattering centres are small compared to the wavelength of the radiation the elastic scattering is called Rayleigh scattering and Mie scattering if this condition is not fulfilled.

candidates.label: scattering_angle
candidates.definition: The scattering angle is that between the direction of the beam of incident radiation and the direction into which it is scattered.

candidates.label: small-angle X-ray scattering data
candidates.definition: Data which is obtained from an X-ray scattering experiment where the X-rays are scattered by the sample at low angles (0–10°).

candidates.label: two-dimensional small-angle X-ray scattering data
candidates.definition: Data which is obtained from an X-ray scattering experiment where two separate beams of X-rays scattered by a sample at low angles (0–10 deg).

candidates.label: scattering data
candidates.definition: Data which is obtained from a scattering experiment.

candidates.label: Scattering Angle
candidates.definition: The angle which spans between the tangent of the incoming trajectory of an particle and the the tangent of the outgoing trajectory of the same particle, prior and past an instance of scattering.

candidates.label: data point
candidates.definition: A data point is the single point in a coordinate space. [Allotrope]

candidates.label: 2D-data point
candidates.definition: A 2D-data point is a data point in 2-dimensional space. [Allotrope]

candidates.label: 3D-data point
candidates.definition: A 3D-data point is a data point in 3-dimensional space. [Allotrope]

candidates.label: input data
candidates.definition: It identifies whether the data has been normalized (by Z and Z' factors, signal to background, signal to noise, and coefficient of variance), or if it was an immediate readout obtained from a HTS assay.

candidates.label: normalized data
candidates.definition: Data can be normalized by Z and Z' factors, signal to background, signal to noise, and coefficient of variance. Plate based normalization is usually based on controls. In the absence of controls, the Z-score can be used to normalize the data by plate.

candidates.label: raw data
candidates.definition: The readout obtained from a HTS assay which includes measurements from the positive and negative control wells in each plate. This is the data that needs to be processed.

candidates.label: Aggregated data item
candidates.definition: Set of data (either measurement or result data) that constitutes a logical grouped entity for the purpsose of deriving additional information (visual, textual, or numeric). For example, calibration data.

candidates.label: Calibration data
candidates.definition: A set of data from the analysis of a set of standard materials aggregated in order to derive the relationship between the independent and dependent variables.

candidates.label: Replicate data
candidates.definition: A group of data points that are nominally the same numeric value becuase they are equally valid estimates of a property of the same population, but due to random error will be scattered based on the distrubution model applicable in the context of process of measuring the data.

candidates.label: Text data file
candidates.definition: Text based data file that can be in a number of delimited, e.g. CSV, JSON, standardized e.g. JCAMP, MOL, XML or freeform formats

candidates.label: Exemplar data item
candidates.definition: Example datum, data or data arrays that are used to show the quality/capbilities of a chemical analysis methodology

candidates.label: crystallographic data
candidates.definition: Data which is obtained from a diffraction experiment.

candidates.label: electron diffraction data
candidates.definition: Data which is obtained from an electron diffraction experiment.

candidates.label: neutron diffraction data
candidates.definition: Data which is obtained from a neutron diffraction experiment.

candidates.label: structure data
candidates.definition: Data obtained from a structure determination method.

candidates.label: scattering data
candidates.definition: Data which is obtained from a scattering experiment.

candidates.label: Data curation
candidates.definition: Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data (including software code, where it is necessary for interpreting the data itself) for initial use and later re-use.

candidates.label: Data
candidates.definition: Research data or artifacts.

candidates.label: Anonymised Data
candidates.definition: Personal Data that has been (fully and completely) anonymised so that it is no longer considered Personal Data

candidates.label: Collected Data
candidates.definition: Data that has been obtained by collecting it from a source

candidates.label: Collected Personal Data
candidates.definition: Personal Data that has been collected from another source such as the Data Subject

candidates.label: Commercially Confidential Data
candidates.definition: Data that is considered confidential due to business/trade secrets, confidentiality agreements, or company secrets

candidates.label: Confidential Data
candidates.definition: Data deemed confidential

candidates.label: Contextually Anonymised Data
candidates.definition: Data that can be considered as being fully anonymised within the context but in actuality is not fully anonymised and is still personal data as it can be de-anonymised outside that context

candidates.label: Data
candidates.definition: A broad concept representing 'data' or 'information'

candidates.label: Data Altruism
candidates.definition: Purposes associated with the voluntary sharing of data for the general interest of the public, such as healthcare or combating climate change

candidates.label: Data Availability Assessment
candidates.definition: Measures associated with assessment of availability of data for specific task(s)

candidates.label: Data Backup Protocols
candidates.definition: Protocols or plans for backing up of data

candidates.label: Data Breach Notice
candidates.definition: A notice providing information about data breach(es) i.e. unauthorised transfer, access, use, or modification of data

candidates.label: Data Breach Notification
candidates.definition: Notification of information about data breach(es) i.e. unauthorised transfer, access, use, or modification of data

candidates.label: Data Breach Record
candidates.definition: Record of a data breach incident

candidates.label: Data Controller
candidates.definition: The individual or organisation that decides (or controls) the purpose(s) of processing personal data.

candidates.label: Data Controller Contract
candidates.definition: Creation, completion, fulfilment, or performance of a contract, with Data Controllers as parties being Joint Data Controllers, and involving specified processing of data or technologies. NOTE: This concept is being deprecated - use dpv:JointDataControllersAgreement which has a more explicit definition of the entities involved and the intent of the contract

candidates.label: Data Controller as Data Source
candidates.definition: Data Sourced from Data Controller(s), e.g. a Controller inferring data or generating data

candidates.label: Data Deletion Policy
candidates.definition: Policy regarding deletion of data

candidates.label: Data Erasure Policy
candidates.definition: Policy regarding erasure of data

candidates.label: Data Exporter
candidates.definition: An entity that 'exports' data where exporting is considered a form of data transfer

candidates.label: Data Governance
candidates.definition: Measures associated with topics typically considered to be part of 'Data Governance'

candidates.label: Data Handling Clause
candidates.definition: Contractual clauses governing handling of data within or by an entity

candidates.label: Data Importer
candidates.definition: An entity that 'imports' data where importing is considered a form of data transfer

candidates.label: Data Interoperability Assessment
candidates.definition: Measures associated with assessment of data interoperability

candidates.label: Data Interoperability Improvement
candidates.definition: Measures associated with improvement of data interoperability

candidates.label: Data Interoperability Management
candidates.definition: Measures associated with management of data interoperability

candidates.label: Data Inventory Management
candidates.definition: Measures associated with management of data inventory or a data asset list

candidates.label: Data Jurisdiction Policy
candidates.definition: Policy specifying jurisdictional requirements for data processing

candidates.label: Data Literacy
candidates.definition: Providing skills, knowledge, and understanding to enable reading, writing, analysing, reasoning, and communicating regarding data

candidates.label: Data Processing Agreement
candidates.definition: An agreement outlining conditions, criteria, obligations, responsibilities, and specifics for carrying out processing of data

candidates.label: Data Processing Policy
candidates.definition: Policy regarding data processing activities

candidates.label: Data Processing Record
candidates.definition: Record of data processing, whether ex-ante or ex-post

candidates.label: Data Processor
candidates.definition: A ‘processor’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes data on behalf of the controller.

candidates.label: Data Processor Contract
candidates.definition: Creation, completion, fulfilment, or performance of a contract, with the Data Controller and Data Processor as parties, and involving specified processing of data or technologies. NOTE: This concept is being deprecated - use dpv:ControllerProcessorAgreement which has a more explicit definition of the entities involved and the intent of the contract

candidates.label: Data Protection Authority
candidates.definition: An authority tasked with overseeing legal compliance regarding privacy and data protection laws.

candidates.label: Data Protection Officer
candidates.definition: An entity within or authorised by an organisation to monitor internal compliance, inform and advise on data protection obligations and act as a contact point for data subjects and the supervisory authority.

candidates.label: Data Protection Training
candidates.definition: Training intended to increase knowledge regarding data protection

candidates.label: Data published by Data Subject
candidates.definition: Data is published by the data subject

candidates.label: Data Quality Assessment
candidates.definition: Measures associated with assessment of data quality

candidates.label: Data Quality Improvement
candidates.definition: Measures associated with improvement of data quality

candidates.label: Data Quality Management
candidates.definition: Measures associated with management of data quality

candidates.label: Data Redaction
candidates.definition: Removal of sensitive information from a data or document

candidates.label: Data Restoration Policy
candidates.definition: Policy regarding restoration of data

candidates.label: Data Reuse Policy
candidates.definition: Policy regarding reuse of data i.e. using data for purposes other than its initial purpose

candidates.label: Data Sanitisation Technique
candidates.definition: Cleaning or any removal or re-organisation of elements in data based on selective criteria

candidates.label: Data Security Management
candidates.definition: Measures associated with management of data security

candidates.label: Data Source
candidates.definition: The source or origin of data

candidates.label: Data Storage Policy
candidates.definition: Policy regarding storage of data, including the manner, duration, location, and conditions for storage

candidates.label: Data Sub-Processor
candidates.definition: A 'sub-processor' is a processor engaged by another processor

candidates.label: Data Subject
candidates.definition: The individual (or category of individuals) whose personal data is being processed

candidates.label: Data Subject Contract
candidates.definition: Creation, completion, fulfilment, or performance of a contract, with the Data Controller and Data Subject as parties, and involving specified processing of data or technologies. NOTE: This concept is being deprecated - use dpv:ControllerDataSubjectAgreement which has a more explicit definition of the entities involved and the intent of the contract

candidates.label: Data Subject as Data Source
candidates.definition: Data Sourced from Data Subject(s), e.g. when data is collected via a form or observed from their activities

candidates.label: Data Subject Informed
candidates.definition: Status indicating DataSubject has been informed about the specified context

candidates.label: Data Subject Right
candidates.definition: The rights applicable or provided to a Data Subject

candidates.label: Data Subject Scale
candidates.definition: Scale of Data Subject(s)

candidates.label: Data Subject Uninformed
candidates.definition: Status indicating DataSubject is uninformed i.e. has not been informed about the specified context

candidates.label: Data Suitability Assessment
candidates.definition: Measures associated with assessment of suitability of data for specific task(s)

candidates.label: Data Transfer Notice
candidates.definition: Notice for the legal entity for the transfer of its data

candidates.label: Data Transfer Record
candidates.definition: Record of data transfer activities

candidates.label: Data Volume
candidates.definition: Volume or Scale of Data

candidates.label: Derived Data
candidates.definition: Data that has been obtained through derivations of other data

candidates.label: Derived Personal Data
candidates.definition: Personal Data that is obtained or derived from other data

candidates.label: Elderly Data Subject
candidates.definition: Data subjects that are considered elderly (i.e. based on age)

candidates.label: Generated Data
candidates.definition: Data that is generated or brought into existence without relation to existing data i.e. it is not derived or inferred from other data

candidates.label: Generated Personal Data
candidates.definition: Personal Data that is generated or brought into existence without relation to existing data i.e. it is not derived or inferred from other data

candidates.label: Huge Data Volume
candidates.definition: Data volume that is considered huge or more than large within the context

candidates.label: Identifying Personal Data
candidates.definition: Personal Data that explicitly and by itself is sufficient to identify a person

candidates.label: Incorrect Data
candidates.definition: Data that is known to be incorrect or inconsistent with some requirements

candidates.label: Inferred Data
candidates.definition: Data that has been obtained through inferences of other data

candidates.label: Inferred Personal Data
candidates.definition: Personal Data that is obtained through inference from other data

candidates.label: Intellectual Property Data
candidates.definition: Data protected by Intellectual Property rights and regulations

candidates.label: Joint Data Controllers
candidates.definition: A group of Data Controllers that jointly determine the purposes and means of processing

candidates.label: Large Data Volume
candidates.definition: Data volume that is considered large within the context

candidates.label: Medium Data Volume
candidates.definition: Data volume that is considered medium i.e. neither large nor small within the context

candidates.label: Non-Personal Data
candidates.definition: Data that is not Personal Data

candidates.label: Observed Data
candidates.definition: Data that has been obtained through observations of a source

candidates.label: Observed Personal Data
candidates.definition: Personal Data that has been collected through observation of the Data Subject(s)

candidates.label: Personal Data
candidates.definition: Data directly or indirectly associated or related to an individual

candidates.label: Personal Data Audit
candidates.definition: An audit that systematically examines the existence and use of personal data along with its associated resources (e.g. where it is stored) and flows (e.g. where it originates and with whom it is being shared)

candidates.label: Personal Data Handling
candidates.definition: An abstract concept describing 'personal data handling'

candidates.label: Provided Data
candidates.definition: Data that has been provided by an entity

candidates.label: Pseudonymised Data
candidates.definition: Pseudonymised Data is data that has gone a partial or incomplete anonymisation process by replacing the identifiable information with artificial identifiers or 'pseudonyms', and is still considered as personal data

candidates.label: Sensitive Data
candidates.definition: Data deemed sensitive

candidates.label: Synthetic Data
candidates.definition: Synthetic data refers to artificially created data such that it is intended to resemble real data (personal or non-personal), but does not refer to any specific identified or identifiable individual, or to the real measure of an observable parameter in the case of non-personal data

candidates.label: Uncategorised Data
candidates.definition: Data whose categorisation is not known e.g. whether it is personal or non-personal data

candidates.label: Unstructured Data
candidates.definition: Data that is without a predefined data model or is not organised in a pre-defined manner

candidates.label: Unverified Data
candidates.definition: Data that has not been verified in terms of accuracy, inconsistency, or quality

candidates.label: Verified Data
candidates.definition: Data that has been verified in terms of accuracy, consistency, or quality

candidates.label: has data
candidates.definition: Indicates associated with Data (may or may not be personal)

candidates.label: Customer Data
candidates.definition: CUSTOMER DATA includes all information necessary to manage orders—such as identifiers, addresses, logistics preferences, and contractual conditions.

candidates.label: Supplier Data
candidates.definition: Information about a supplier.

candidates.label: Environmental Data
candidates.definition: Additional information to a process like work schedule, production plans, etc.

candidates.label: data use permission
candidates.definition: A data item that is used to indicate consent permissions for datasets and/or materials, and relates to the purposes for which datasets and/or material might be removed, stored or used.

candidates.label: data use modifier
candidates.definition: Data use modifiers indicate additional conditions for use.

candidates.label: Data
candidates.definition: Information, represented in an information artefact (data record) that is 'understandable' by dedicated computational tools that can use the data as input or produce it as output.

candidates.label: Sequence signature data
candidates.definition: Sequence signature data concerns specific or conserved pattern in molecular sequences and the classifiers used for their identification, including sequence motifs, profiles or other diagnostic element.

candidates.label: Phylogenetic character data
candidates.definition: Basic character data from which a phylogenetic tree may be generated.

candidates.label: Protein interaction data
candidates.definition: Data concerning the interactions (predicted or known) within or between a protein, structural domain or part of a protein. This includes intra- and inter-residue contacts and distances, as well as interactions with other proteins and non-protein entities such as nucleic acid, metal atoms, water, ions etc.

candidates.label: Codon usage data
candidates.definition: Data derived from analysis of codon usage (typically a codon usage table) of DNA sequences.

candidates.label: Raw NMR data
candidates.definition: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) raw data, typically for a protein.

candidates.label: Data index
candidates.definition: An index of data of biological relevance.

candidates.label: Data index report
candidates.definition: A human-readable collection of information concerning an analysis of an index of biological data.

candidates.label: Ontology concept data
candidates.definition: Data concerning or derived from a concept from a biological ontology.

candidates.label: Phylogenetic discrete data
candidates.definition: Character data with discrete states that may be read during phylogenetic tree calculation.

candidates.label: Peptide immunogenicity data
candidates.definition: An report on allergenicity / immunogenicity of peptides and proteins.

candidates.label: Map data
candidates.definition: Data describing a molecular map (genetic or physical) or a set of such maps, including various attributes of, data extracted from or derived from the analysis of them, but excluding the map(s) themselves. This includes metadata for map sets that share a common set of features which are mapped.

candidates.label: Enzyme kinetics data
candidates.definition: Data concerning chemical reaction(s) catalysed by enzyme(s).

candidates.label: Data reference
candidates.definition: Reference to a dataset (or a cross-reference between two datasets), typically one or more entries in a biological database or ontology.

candidates.label: Ontology data
candidates.definition: Data concerning or derived from an ontology.

candidates.label: Phylogenetic data
candidates.definition: Data concerning phylogeny, typically of molecular sequences, including reports of information concerning or derived from a phylogenetic tree, or from comparing two or more phylogenetic trees.

candidates.label: Text data
candidates.definition: Data concerning, extracted from, or derived from the analysis of a scientific text (or texts) such as a full text article from a scientific journal.

candidates.label: Mass spectrometry data
candidates.definition: Data concerning a mass spectrometry measurement.

candidates.label: Expression data
candidates.definition: Image, hybridisation or some other data arising from a study of feature/molecule expression, typically profiling or quantification.

candidates.label: Protein hydropathy data
candidates.definition: A report on protein properties concerning hydropathy.

candidates.label: Reaction data
candidates.definition: Data concerning a biochemical reaction, typically data and more general annotation on the kinetics of enzyme-catalysed reaction.

candidates.label: Protein geometry data
candidates.definition: Geometry data for a protein structure, for example bond lengths, bond angles, torsion angles, chiralities, planaraties etc.

candidates.label: Raw microarray data
candidates.definition: Raw data (typically MIAME-compliant) for hybridisations from a microarray experiment.

candidates.label: Processed microarray data
candidates.definition: Data generated from processing and analysis of probe set data from a microarray experiment.

candidates.label: Microarray hybridisation data
candidates.definition: Data concerning the hybridisations measured during a microarray experiment.

candidates.label: Biodiversity data
candidates.definition: Machine-readable biodiversity data.

candidates.label: Ecological data
candidates.definition: Data concerning ecology; for example measurements and reports from the study of interactions among organisms and their environment.

candidates.label: Alpha diversity data
candidates.definition: The mean species diversity in sites or habitats at a local scale.

candidates.label: Beta diversity data
candidates.definition: The ratio between regional and local species diversity.

candidates.label: Gamma diversity data
candidates.definition: The total species diversity in a landscape.

candidates.label: Over-representation data
candidates.definition: A ranked list of categories (usually ontology concepts), each associated with a statistical metric of over-/under-representation within the studied data.

candidates.label: Molecular simulation data
candidates.definition: Data coming from molecular simulations, computer "experiments" on model molecules.

candidates.label: Trajectory data
candidates.definition: Dynamic information of a structure molecular system coming from a molecular simulation: XYZ 3D coordinates (sometimes with their associated velocities) for every atom along time.

candidates.label: Topology data
candidates.definition: Static information of a structure molecular system that is needed for a molecular simulation: the list of atoms, their non-bonded parameters for Van der Waals and electrostatic interactions, and the complete connectivity in terms of bonds, angles and dihedrals.

candidates.label: Pathway overrepresentation data
candidates.definition: A ranked list of pathways, each associated with z-score, p-value or similar, concerning or derived from the analysis of e.g. a set of genes or proteins.

candidates.label: Data management plan
candidates.definition: Data management plan is a document describing the data management of a project or an organisation, including acquisition, reuse, structure, processing, storage, documentation, sharing, and preservation of data. This may include budgeting for these operations.

candidates.label: Chemical data format
candidates.definition: Format of a report on a chemical compound.

candidates.label: Data index format
candidates.definition: Format of a data index of some type.

candidates.label: Biodiversity data format
candidates.definition: Data format for biodiversity data.

candidates.label: Linked data format
candidates.definition: A linked data format enables publishing structured data as linked data (Linked Data), so that the data can be interlinked and become more useful through semantic queries.

candidates.label: NMR data format
candidates.definition: Data format for raw data from a nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy experiment.

candidates.label: Data visualisation
candidates.definition: Rendering (drawing on a computer screen) or visualisation of molecular sequences, structures or other biomolecular data.

candidates.label: Data management
candidates.definition: Data management comprises the practices and principles of taking care of data, other than analysing them. This includes for example taking care of the associated metadata, data formats, storage, preservation/archiving, access, and legal aspects related to using and sharing data.

candidates.label: Data acquisition
candidates.definition: The acquisition of data, typically measurements of physical systems using any type of sampling system, or by another other means.

candidates.label: Data mining
candidates.definition: The discovery of patterns in large data sets and the extraction and trasnsformation of those patterns into a useful format.

candidates.label: Data governance
candidates.definition: Data governance is the control of data entry and maintenance to ensure the data meets defined standards, qualities, or constraints.

candidates.label: Data quality management
candidates.definition: The quality, integrity, and cleaning up of data.

candidates.label: Data rescue
candidates.definition: Data rescue denotes digitalisation, formatting, archival, and publication of data that were not available in accessible or usable form. Examples are data from private archives, data inside publications, or in paper records stored privately or publicly.

candidates.label: FAIR data
candidates.definition: FAIR data is scientific data that meets the principles of being findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable.

candidates.label: Data protection
candidates.definition: Data protection is a topic concerning data that should be protected from disclosure, damage, or unauthorised access, due to its sensitive nature.

candidates.label: Data
candidates.definition: A perspective in which entities are represented according to the variation of their properties.

candidates.label: data file
candidates.definition: A realisation of a fabio:Dataset (a frbr:Work) containing a defined collection of data with specific content and possibly with a specific version number, that can be embodied as a fabio:DigitalManifestation (a frbr:Manifestation with a specific format) and be represented by a specific fabio:ComputerFile (a frbr:Item) on someone's hard drive.

candidates.label: data repository
candidates.definition: A repository for storing data.

candidates.label: data entity
candidates.definition: An information content entity that is intended to be one or more truthful statement(s) about something (modulo, e.g., measurement precision or other systematic errors) and is constructed/acquired by a method which reliably tends to produce (approximately) truthful statements.

candidates.label: data collection
candidates.definition: A data entity that consists of multiple data entities.

candidates.label: Data representation
candidates.definition: Physical representation of (structured) data.

candidates.label: Data Resource
candidates.definition: Resource (at least partially) comprising data content.

candidates.label: Data Processing (Integrated Data)
candidates.definition: Class representing the execution of a particular computer code which extracts/reshapes/processes data from one form to another. The data is the result of processing raw data from a Sensofar Optical Surface Profilometer and an Optimol tribometer.

candidates.label: Data Processing (Optimol Data)
candidates.definition: Class representing the execution of a particular computer code which extracts/reshapes/processes data from one form to another. The data stems from an Optimol tribometer.

candidates.label: Data Processing (SEM Data)
candidates.definition: Class representing the execution of a particular computer code/program which extracts/reshapes/processes data from one form to another. The data stems from scanning electron microscopy images.

candidates.label: Data Processing (Topography Data)
candidates.definition: Class representing the execution of a particular computer code which extracts/reshapes/processes data from one form to another. The data stems from an Optical or Tactile Surface Profilometer.

candidates.label: Data Processing
candidates.definition: Class representing the execution of a particular computer code which extracts/reshapes/processes data from one form to another.

candidates.label: Data Published
candidates.definition: Is the data available?

candidates.label: Data Publication
candidates.definition: This is a representation of the digital records which can be found online and contain part of the data/metadata of the records in the same collection.

candidates.label: Processed Data
candidates.definition: Data processing occurs when data is collected and translated into usable information.

candidates.label: Raw Data
candidates.definition: Raw data, oftentimes referred to as source or primary data, is data that hasn’t been processed, coded, formatted, or yet analyzed for useful information.

candidates.label: Data Mining
candidates.definition: Data mining is the process of discovering patterns in large data sets involving methods at the intersection of machine learning, statistics, and database systems.

candidates.label: data transformation
candidates.definition: Terms used to describe types of data processing.

candidates.label: Data Explorer
candidates.definition: Applied Biosystems software for data acquisition and analysis.

candidates.label: low intensity data point removal
candidates.definition: The removal of very low intensity data points that are likely to be spurious noise rather than real signal.

candidates.label: high intensity data point removal
candidates.definition: The removal of very high intensity data points.

candidates.label: data filtering
candidates.definition: Filtering out part of the data.

candidates.label: Original data
candidates.definition: One dataset is not a reanalysis of previously published data.

candidates.label: deconvoluted data
candidates.definition: The data contained in this file have been processed to remove, collapse, or label one or more dimensions of the original dataset, such as charge deconvolution or ion mobility deconvolution. To determine the type of deconvolution done, the reader should consult the appropriate section of the file, such as the data processing methods in an mzML file.

candidates.label: data encoding
candidates.definition: a documenting process to encode an information entity into a digital document

candidates.label: sequence data
candidates.definition: A data item that representing the primary structure of a macromolecule(it's sequence) sometimes associated with an indicator of confidence of that measurement.

candidates.label: data service
candidates.definition: A service that has some information content entity as input and output.

candidates.label: data transformation
candidates.definition: A completely executed planned process that produces output data from input data.

candidates.label: data imputation
candidates.definition: Imputation is a means of filling in missing data values from a predictive distribution of the missing values.  The predictive distribution can be created either based on a formal statistical model (i,e, a multivariate normal distribution) or an algorithm.

candidates.label: data visualization
candidates.definition: A planned process with the objective to graphically represent some data by inputing the data and outputting images, diagrams or animations.

candidates.label: data combination
candidates.definition: A data transformation in which individual input data elements and values are merged together into a output set of data elements and values.

candidates.label: data partitioning
candidates.definition: Data partitioning is a data transformation with the objective of partitioning or separating input data into output subsets.

candidates.label: data vector reduction data transformation
candidates.definition: A data vector reduction is a data transformation that has objective data vector reduction and that consists of reducing the input vectors k to a smaller number of output vectors j, where j<k.

candidates.label: data descriptor
candidates.definition: A data descriptor is an information content entity that contains additional information about some data.

candidates.label: data format
candidates.definition: A data format is a data descriptor that specifies the structure in which the data item is encoded.

candidates.label: data postprocessing
candidates.definition: Data postprocessing is data processing that transforms the output of a model calculation into a form that is suitable for presentation.

candidates.label: data preprocessing
candidates.definition: Data preprocessing is data processing that transforms the input into a form that is useable for a model calculation.

candidates.label: data processing
candidates.definition: data processing is a transformation in which a data item gets transformed.

candidates.label: output data
candidates.definition: Output data is endogenous data that is determined by a model calculation and presented as a result.

candidates.label: data licence
candidates.definition: A data licence is a licence that determines ownership, database protection, and permissions for data.

candidates.label: exogenous data
candidates.definition: Exogenous data is a data item whose quantity value is determined outside of a model and is imposed on a model.

candidates.label: endogenous data
candidates.definition: Endogenous data is a data item whose quantity value is determined by a model.

candidates.label: data center
candidates.definition: A datacenter is an artificial object that houses computer systems and associated components.

candidates.label: data preparation
candidates.definition: Data preparation is an action specification that describes the steps the bearer takes to acquire raw data and how this data is cleaned, transformed, and structured for subsequent analysis. So it includes the acquisition and pre-processing of data.

candidates.label: Data report
candidates.definition: These reports are used to report actual data that may be measured or calculated.

candidates.label: Annotated data
candidates.definition: Experimental data with additional information or labels assigned to them

candidates.label: Data
candidates.definition: Information collected for use

candidates.label: Data format
candidates.definition:
The definition of the structure of data within a database or file system that gives the information its meaning
(https://c3.ai/glossary/features/data-format/)

candidates.label: Data repository
candidates.definition: A space or location where data is stored

candidates.label: Data type
candidates.definition: specific category of data

candidates.label: Digital data
candidates.definition: Data that exist in digital environments, e.g. digital files

candidates.label: Image data
candidates.definition: Data produced by scanning a surface with an optical or electronic device; visual information in the form of pictures, graphics or photographs

candidates.label: Input data
candidates.definition: Data provided as input to a laboratory process, experiment, measurement or device to produce desired outcomes

candidates.label: Numeric data
candidates.definition: Data consisting of numerical values representing measurements or quantities

candidates.label: Output data
candidates.definition: Data generated by a device or produced as a result of a laboratory process, experiment, measurement, data analysis and other data tranformations

candidates.label: Physical data
candidates.definition: Data in the form of physical objects, e.g. paper files

candidates.label: Processed data
candidates.definition: Data derived from raw data through various transformations, calculations, filtering or other operations

candidates.label: Raw data
candidates.definition: Original, unprocessed data collected directly from experiment

candidates.label: Secure data
candidates.definition: Data with sensitive or confidential content that needs to be protected from unauthorised access, loss, or alteration

candidates.label: Data Encoding
candidates.definition: Data Encoding expresses the properties that specify how data is represented at the bit and byte level. These properties are applicable to describing raw data.

candidates.label: Data Item
candidates.definition: A Data Item holds a value that maybe a scalar or structured datatype. Quantity Value specifies which case applies.

candidates.label: Data Encoding
candidates.definition: Data Encoding expresses the properties that specify how data is represented at the bit and byte level. These properties are applicable to describing raw data.

candidates.label: Data point
candidates.definition:
A data point is a quantity that is extended with various pieces of process information, namely
 
- A creation time (instant). This is the point in time when the data point was created, which is not necessarily the time for which it is valid. In the case of soft-sensors or forecasters, a data point might have been created ahead of time, in the case of a direct observation a data point might created at its time of validity (or at the end of its validity time interval) and in the case of an archived value the data point might have been created after the fact.

 - A validity time (temporal entity) which will be named "time stamp". The validity time is the instant or interval in time in which a specific quantity is in effect. For example a room temperature might be measured at 12:00, which means it is in effect at this very instant. A specific amount of energy might me expended within the time-slot between 12:30 and 12:45, which means that the energy observation is in effect during this time interval.

 - A location or topological association. For example, an observation might be taken in a specific room, a power avarage might have been measured by a specific meter, a forecast might be valid for a specific region or grid segment. This association is therefore not always a location.

candidates.label: Gaussian data point
candidates.definition: A data point whose quantity is a standard deviation.

candidates.label: Data Transformation
candidates.definition: Class that represents a software for performing data transformation.

candidates.label: data item
candidates.definition: A data item consists of information that has been collected/generated towards some purpose.

candidates.label: data series
candidates.definition: A data series is a data set composed of related values displayed in a statistical graph.

candidates.label: data point
candidates.definition: A data point is a point that which corresponds to the projection of the values of measurement data against the axes of a statistical graph.

candidates.label: scientific data
candidates.definition: scientific data is data obtained from some scientific procedure.

candidates.label: data transformation
candidates.definition: data transformation is the process of applying an algorithmic procedure to some input data and producing some output data.

candidates.label: data analysis
candidates.definition: data analysis is a process of inspecting, cleaning, transforming, and modeling data with the goal of highlighting useful information, suggesting conclusions, and supporting decision making.

candidates.label: data collection
candidates.definition: data collection is the process of acquiring information.

candidates.label: biological data
candidates.definition: biological data is scientific data relevant to biology.

candidates.label: genetic data
candidates.definition: genetic data is data pertaining to genetics.

candidates.label: bioinformatic data
candidates.definition: bioinformatic data is data genereated or used for computer-based investigations of biological phenomena.

candidates.label: medical data
candidates.definition: medical data is data of interest to medicine.

candidates.label: data munging
candidates.definition: A series of potentially destructive or irrevocable changes to a piece of data or a file. Common munging operations include removing punctuation or html tags, data parsing, filtering, and transformation.

candidates.label: data registration
candidates.definition: Curation process on a data object by which it receives a persistent identifier (PID) from a trusted registration authority. Registration must be accompanied by the step(s) to create and submit metadata describing the object to the registry.

candidates.label: exposing data
candidates.definition: Exposing data is the activity of exposing your data to collaborators, the public, or other interested parties. A data producer makes the data accessible to external users in a machine- and/or human-readable way.

candidates.label: data entity
candidates.definition: Object, event or phenomenon about which data are stored in a database and which has intermediate representation in a Data Model.

candidates.label: data processing
candidates.definition: Generic concept referring to all kinds of procedures being executed on data at any point in the data lifecycle.

candidates.label: data organization
candidates.definition: Set of measures that are used by a repository to form aggregations of data objects (including collections and metadata) to describe the properties of data objects, to register PIDs, to build the PID records, to link between all components, and to set up the containers (in the form of the software stack) that are used to store all components.

candidates.label: data rescue
candidates.definition: Recovery and/or transformation and digitization of dark data and at-risk data so that they can be preserved, accessed, shared, and used. Data rescue also involves the addition of rich metadata to make the content understandable and more easily re-usable.

candidates.label: data warehouse
candidates.definition: Central repository for all or significant parts of the data that an organisation’s various business systems collect, containing harmonised, highly-structured, quality data integrated from multiple sources. Data warehousing emphasises the capture of data from diverse sources for useful analysis and access, but does not generally start from the point-of-view of the end user who may need access to specialised data marts. There are two approaches to data warehousing: The top-down approach spins off data marts for specific groups of users after the complete data warehouse has been created. The bottom-up approach builds the data marts first and then combines them into a single, all-encompassing data warehouse.

candidates.label: data identifier
candidates.definition: An identifier that uniquely distinguishes one set of data from all others.

candidates.label: data splitting
candidates.definition: Protecting sensitive data from unauthorised access by encrypting the data and storing different portions of a file on different servers. An unauthorised person would need to know the locations of the servers containing the parts, be able to get access to each server, know what data to combine, and how to decrypt it. Data splitting can be made even more effective by periodically retrieving and recombining the parts, and then splitting the data in a different way among different servers, and using a different encryption key.

candidates.label: data modeling
candidates.definition: Formalising and documenting existing processes and events. A first step in analysing a system of objects with which users interact is to identify each object and its relationship to other objects. This process is called data modelling and results in a picture of object relationships. Data modellers often use multiple models to view the same data and ensure that all processes, entities, relationships and data flows have been identified. There are several different approaches to data modelling, including: Conceptual Data Modelling (identifies the highest-level relationships between different entities); Enterprise Data Modelling (similar to conceptual data modelling, but addresses the unique requirements of a specific organisation); Logical Data Modelling (illustrates the specific entities, attributes and relationships involved in a business function. Serves as the basis for the creation of the physical data model); Physical Data Modelling (represents an application and database-specific implementation of a logical data model).

candidates.label: data transformation
candidates.definition: Manipulation of raw data to produce a single output.

candidates.label: data dictionary
candidates.definition: Collection of descriptions of the data objects or items in a data model. After each data object or item is given a descriptive name, its relationship is described (or it becomes part of some structure that implicitly describes relationship), the type of data (such as text or image or binary value) is described, possible predefined values are listed, and a brief textual description is provided. This collection can be organised for reference into a data dictionary.

candidates.label: data selection
candidates.definition: Process that creates a new dataset from an original source.

candidates.label: data discovery
candidates.definition: The ability to find and comprehend data produced by people other than yourself.

candidates.label: documented data
candidates.definition: Data that are delivered with all associated metadata, data dictionary, description of methods and instruments used to collect and process the data, and other supporting data (such as duplicate sample results, replicate analyses, percent recovery, etc.) with the purpose of providing the full context in which the data were created.

candidates.label: dynamic data
candidates.definition: Data that are changing frequently and at asynchronous moments.

candidates.label: registered data
candidates.definition: Data that have gone through a registration process and have been assigned an identifier metadata to aid in their search and retrieval.

candidates.label: data catalogue
candidates.definition: Curated collection of metadata records describing datasets and their data elements. Curated and organised using a formal metadata schema appropriate to data and data sets (e.g. ReCollect etc).

candidates.label: publish data
candidates.definition: AL 9.3.22. Removed from 'FAIR4S defined activity' class to better integrate with the T4FS hierarchy. AL 5.5.22: removed "Publishing and archiving data" and "Publish and archive data" alternative terms, as the two actions are not the same.

candidates.label: data production
candidates.definition: All activities involved in the planning, collecting, processing, analysis and maintenance of data in the original research project. Among these activities are selecting a study design, constructing instruments for data collection, conducting data collection/creation, performing data editing/verification/validation, analysing data, backing up data versions and preparing and tagging metadata.

candidates.label: raw data
candidates.definition: Data that have not been processed for meaningful use. Although raw data have the potential to become information, they require selective extraction, organisation, and sometimes analysis and formatting for presentation.

candidates.label: data compliance
candidates.definition: Ongoing processes to ensure adherence of data to both enterprise business rules (government department, university, industry, or agency), and to legal, regulatory and accreditation requirements. Includes five areas: controls, audit, legal compliance, regulatory compliance, and accreditation conformance.

candidates.label: data curation
candidates.definition: Managed process throughout the data lifecycle, by which data/data collections are cleansed, documented, standardised, formatted and inter-related. This includes versioning data, or forming a new collection from several data sources, annotating with metadata, adding codes to raw data (e.g., classifying a galaxy image with a galaxy type such as “spiral”). Higher levels of curation involve maintaining links with annotation and with other published materials. Thus a dataset may include a citation link to publication whose analysis was based on the data. The goal of curation is to manage and promote the use of data from its point of creation to ensure it is fit for contemporary purpose and available for discovery and re-use. For dynamic datasets this may mean continuous enrichment or updating to keep it fit for purpose. Special forms of curation may be available in data repositories. The data curation process itself must be documented as part of curation. Thus curation and provenance are highly related.

candidates.label: data management
candidates.definition: The activities of data policies, data planning, data element standardization, information management control, data synchronization, data sharing, and database development, including practices and projects that acquire, control, protect, deliver and enhance the value of data and information.

candidates.label: data structure
candidates.definition: Specialised format for organising and storing data. General data structure types include the array, the file, the record, the table, the tree, and so on. Any data structure is designed to organise data to suit a specific purpose so that it can be accessed and worked with in appropriate ways. In computer programming, a data structure may be selected or designed to store data for the purpose of working on it with various algorithms.

candidates.label: data destruction
candidates.definition: Process of destroying data stored on tapes, hard disks and other forms of electronic media so that it is completely unreadable and cannot be accessed or used.

candidates.label: data table attribute
candidates.definition: Field or column in a database table. It is an abbreviation for ‘physical data attribute’ which is a single data element related to a data object, such as a table in a database. The database schema associates one or more attributes with each database entity (i.e. table).

candidates.label: data recovery
candidates.definition: The process of restoring data that have been lost, accidentally deleted, corrupted or made inaccessible for any reason. The data recovery process may vary, depending on the circumstances of the data loss, the data recovery software used to create backups, and backup target media. In some cases, end users may be able to restore lost...

candidates.label: data steward
candidates.definition: Data steward is an umbrella term for numerous support roles that involve the creation, management and usage of research data. A data steward facilitates the quality, integrity and access to (meta)data in a manner that is consistent with the appropriate laws and institutional policies, ensuring professional treatment of data throughout all stages of the research project.

candidates.label: data completeness
candidates.definition: Degree to which all required measurements are known. Values may be designated as “missing” in order not to have empty cells, or missing values may be replaced with default or interpolated values. In the case of default or interpolated values, these must be flagged as such to distinguish them from actual measurements or observations. Missing, default, or interpolated values do not imply that the dataset has been made complete.

candidates.label: data stream
candidates.definition: Sequence of digitally encoded, coherent signals used to send or receive a representation of information content as transmitted.

candidates.label: data librarian
candidates.definition: Librarian who manages the sharing and publishing of datasets as openly as possible and as closed as necessary, and the management and curation of repositories required to achieve this. Broad role requirements include support for sharing and publishing datasets, finding, accessing, interoperating and re-using these datasets, reviewing and supporting Data Management Plans and training delivery.

candidates.label: usable data
candidates.definition: Data that can be used: delivered in a form that meets the needs of different end-user audiences, is ready for the tasks that the end-user needs to accomplish, and that has been adapted to the end-user’s needs. Usable data have been cleaned, structured, are in machine readable format, fully documented, and ready for analysis and interpretation.

candidates.label: data lifecycle
candidates.definition: Entire period of time that research data exists. This lifecycle describes the flow of research data starting from planning, collecting, processing, analysing, preserving, sharing and finally reusing the research data. Research data often have a longer lifespan than the research project.

candidates.label: data store
candidates.definition: Repository for persistently storing collections of data, such as a database, a file system or a directory. The data stored can be of any type that can be rendered in digital format and placed in electronic media.

candidates.label: data item
candidates.definition: Type of data element that expresses a proposition that binds one or more property values to some data entity.

candidates.label: data acquisition
candidates.definition: The process of acquiring data from some source. For example, data may be acquired by download from a repository, transfer from a data logger, data capture, etc.

candidates.label: data validation
candidates.definition: Checks that data are valid, sensible, reasonable, clean, usable, and secure before they are processed. Provides well-defined guarantees for fitness, accuracy, and consistency for any of various kinds of user input into an application or automated system. Failures or omissions in data validation can lead to data corruption, security vulnerability. Improperly validated data can cause computer code processing the data to crash, generate error messages, behave in an unanticipated manner, or generate incorrect results that may be difficult or impossible to detect.

candidates.label: data publication
candidates.definition: Release of research data, associated metadata, accompanying documentation, and software code (in cases where the raw data have been processed or manipulated) for re-use and analysis in such a manner that they can be discovered on the Web and referred to in a unique and persistent way. Data publication occurs via dedicated data repositories and/or (data) journals which ensure that the published research objects are findable, accessible, interoperable and re-usable.

candidates.label: citable data
candidates.definition: Standalone dataset that can be cited in a similar manner to other research outputs. The dataset appears in a data repository, data paper or project website, and has a Persistent Identifier. Most current referencing systems provide a format for citing datasets.

candidates.label: big data
candidates.definition: Voluminous amount of structured, semi-structured and/or unstructured data that have the potential to be mined for information, primarily characterised by big volume, extensive variety, high velocity (creation and use), and/or variability that together require a scalable architecture for efficient data storage, manipulation, and analysis. The definition is evolving and can vary by sector, depending on what kind of software tools are commonly available and what sizes of datasets are common in a particular discipline. With those caveats, big data in many sectors today will range from a few dozen terabytes to multiple petabytes.

candidates.label: data archive
candidates.definition: Service providing long-term, permanent care and accessibility for digital objects with research value. The standard for such repositories is the Open Archival Information System reference model.

candidates.label: noisy data
candidates.definition: Meaningless data, including any data that cannot be understood and interpreted correctly by machines such as unstructured text; any data that has been received, stored, or changed in such a manner that it cannot be read or used by the program that originally created it.

candidates.label: data standardization
candidates.definition: Conversion of multiple datasets to a single common format and structure.

candidates.label: open data
candidates.definition: Data that are accessible, machine-readable, usable, intelligible, and freely shared. Open data can be freely used, re-used, built on, and redistributed by anyone – subject only, at most, to the requirement to attribute and sharealike.

candidates.label: curated data
candidates.definition: The output of a data curation activity. Such data has generally already been cleaned, standardised, documented. Additional metadata relevant to the data object has also been added, via either manual or automatic methods.

candidates.label: data custodian
candidates.definition: Individual or organisation responsible for the IT infrastructure providing and protecting data in conformance with the policies and practices prescribed by data governance.

candidates.label: data ingestion
candidates.definition: Process of obtaining, importing, and processing data for later use or storage in a database. This process often involves altering individual files by editing their content and/or formatting them to fit into a larger document. An effective data ingestion methodology begins by validating the individual files, then prioritises the sources for optimum processing, and finally validates the results. When numerous data sources exist in diverse formats (the sources may number in the hundreds and the formats in the dozens), maintaining reasonable speed and efficiency can become a major challenge. To that end, several vendors offer programs tailored to the task of data ingestion in specific applications or environments.

candidates.label: data wrangling
candidates.definition: Manually or semi-automatically converting or mapping data from one form into another format that allows for more convenient consumption of the data with the help of semi-automated tools. Gathering and organising disparate data from different sources, often collected by many different investigators. Activities include developing and supporting search tools that utilise standardised metadata, harmonising the coding of data for specific variables, engineering new methods of combining data. with the help of semi-automated tools. The result of data wrangling is repurposed data.

candidates.label: structured data
candidates.definition: Data elements that have been organised into a consistent format and data structure within a defined data model such that the elements can be easily addressed, organised and accessed in various combinations to make better use of the information, such as in a relational database.

candidates.label: data citation
candidates.definition: Process of citing a dataset in a similar manner to other research outputs. The dataset must be a standalone output that appears in a data repository, data paper or project website, and has a Persistent Identifier. Most current referencing systems provide a format for citing datasets.

candidates.label: data representation
candidates.definition: Object describing the context of the data, including provenance, description, structural, and administrative information.

candidates.label: data residency
candidates.definition: Physical or geographic location of an organisation’s data or information. Data residency also refers to the legal or regulatory requirements imposed on data based on the country or region in which it resides. Cloud computing, which allows organisations to deliver hosted services over the Internet, can create data residency concerns.

candidates.label: data element
candidates.definition: Unit of data for which the definition, identification, representation (term used to represent it), and permissible values are specified by means of a set of attributes.

candidates.label: data policy
candidates.definition: Set of high-level principles that establish a guiding framework for data-related issues. A data policy may contain subsidiary sections that define approaches to strategic aspects such as data access; data protection; data management, custodianship or stewardship; data preservation; relevant legal matters; data acquisition; data ethics and other data-related issues. Distinct from a data management policy which is the subset of data policy addressing the management of a specified set of data assets.

candidates.label: legacy data
candidates.definition: Older data that can no longer be accessed or processed easily because they are stored in obsolete formats or systems.

candidates.label: data integrity
candidates.definition: Assurance that information can only be accessed or modified by those authorised to do so.

candidates.label: data traceability
candidates.definition: Data traceability follows the lifecycle of data to track all access and changes to the data. It helps demonstrate transparency, compliance and adherence to regulations. Data traceability, along with data compliance, can be considered part of a data audit process. Data traceability is fundamental to reproducible research.

candidates.label: data analysis
candidates.definition: Techniques that produce synthesised knowledge from organised information. Process of inspecting, cleaning, transforming, and modelling data with the goal of highlighting useful information suggesting conclusions, and supporting decision making. Data analysis has multiple facets and approaches, encompassing diverse techniques under a variety of names, in different business, science, and social science domains.

candidates.label: data exploration

candidates.label: data mart
candidates.definition: Repository of data designed to serve a particular community of knowledge workers. It's also optimised to support well-known, predefined and repeatable analytic queries, rather than ad-hoc analysis.

candidates.label: data model
candidates.definition: Model that specifies the structure or schema of a dataset. The model provides a documented description of the data and thus is an instance of metadata. It is a logical, relational data model showing an organised dataset as a collection of tables with entity, attributes and relations.

candidates.label: data migration
candidates.definition: Transfer of data between storage types, formats, information technologies, or computer systems. candidates.label: data cleaning
candidates.definition: Process of detecting and correcting corrupt or inaccurate records from a dataset. Data cleaning is a continuous process that requires corrective actions throughout the data lifecycle. Data cleaning involves identifying, replacing, modifying or deleting incomplete, incorrect, inaccurate, inconsistent, irrelevant, and improperly formatted data. Typically, the process involves updating, correcting, standardising, and de-duplicating records to create a single view of the data, even if they are stored in multiple disparate systems.

candidates.label: data reduction

candidates.label: data availability

candidates.label: data review
candidates.definition: Activity through which the correctness conditions of the data are verified. It also includes the specification of the type of the error or condition not met, and the qualification of the data and its division into “error-free” or “erroneous” data. Data review consists of both error detection and data analysis, and can be carried out in manual or automated mode.

candidates.label: data dredging
candidates.definition: Data mining practice in which large volumes of data are analysed seeking any possible relationships between data. The traditional scientific method, in contrast, begins with a hypothesis and follows with an examination of the data. Data dredging often circumvents traditional data mining techniques and may lead to premature conclusions. Uncovered patterns may be presented as statistically significant without any specific hypothesis as to the underlying causality.

candidates.label: unstructured data
candidates.definition: Data that have not been organised into a format and identifiable data structure that makes them easy to access and process. These data can often be searched as long as they are digital, but they are difficult to use for computer analyses.

candidates.label: data linkage
candidates.definition: The process of bringing together from two or more different sources, data that relate to the same individual, family, place or event).

candidates.label: data

candidates.label: repurposed data

candidates.label: data governance

candidates.label: data sharing

candidates.label: data integration

candidates.label: data quality
candidates.definition: Reliability and application efficiency of data. Perception or assessment of a dataset's fitness to serve its purpose in a given context. Aspects of data quality include: Accuracy, Completeness, Update status, Relevance, Consistency across data sources, Reliability, Appropriate presentation, Accessibility. Data quality is affected by the way data are entered, stored and managed. Maintaining data quality requires going through the data periodically and scrubbing it. Typically this involves updating, standardising, and de-duplicating records to create a single view of the data, even if it is stored in multiple disparate systems.

candidates.label: data hygiene

candidates.label: data profiling

The data profiling process cannot identify inaccurate data; it can only identify rule violations and anomalies. The insight gained by data profiling can be used to determine how difficult it will be to use existing data for other purposes. It can also be used to provide metrics to assess data quality and help determine whether or not metadata accurately describes the source data. Profiling tools evaluate the actual content, structure and quality of the data by exploring relationships that exist between value collections both within and across datasets.
