The relative abundance of isotopes in the sample is determined by using an isotope dilution standard (the sample labelled with a rare isotope).

candidates.label: stable isotope ratio mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the relative abundance of non-radioactive isotopes in a sample is determined.

candidates.label: laser desorption-ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser.

candidates.label: laser microprobe mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A laser mass spectrometry in which the sample is vaporised and ionised using a finely focused (<10 um diameter) high-energy pulsed laser.

candidates.label: negative ion laser desorption mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry using negative ionisation where a high-energy pulsed laser is used for sample vaporisation.

candidates.label: positive ion laser desorption mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry using positive ionisation where a high-energy pulsed laser is used for sample vaporisation.

candidates.label: matrix-assisted laser desorption-ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser. The sample is held in a matrix (such as crystallised dihydrobenzoic acid) to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules.

candidates.label: matrix-assisted laser desorption-ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Matrix-assisted laser desorption-ionisation mass spectrometry where the sample ions are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: sol-gel-assisted laser desorption-ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser. The sample is held in a sol-gel matrix to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules.

candidates.label: surface-enhanced laser desorption-ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser. The sample is mixed with a matrix compound (such as crystallised dihydrobenzoic acid) and deposited on a surface, with some chemical functionality, to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-matrix-assisted laser desorption-ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser, and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance. The sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is held in a matrix (such as dihydrobenzoic acid) to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry in which a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography.

candidates.label: photoionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is irradiated with an ultraviolet laser. The sample absorbs one or more photons resulting in ionisation.

candidates.label: atmospheric pressure photoionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is irradiated with an ultraviolet laser at atmospheric pressure. The sample absorbs one or more photons resulting in ionisation.

candidates.label: multiphoton ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is irradiated with an ultraviolet laser. The sample absorbs two or more photons resulting in ionisation.

candidates.label: resonance-enhanced multiphoton ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is irradiated with a resonant laser (a laser beam with a wavelength that corresponds to an atomic transition in the sample). The sample absorbs one or more photons resulting in ionisation.

candidates.label: resonance ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is irradiated with a resonant laser (a laser beam with a wavelength that corresponds to an atomic transition in the sample). The sample absorbs two or more photons resulting in ionisation.

candidates.label: sonic spray mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where ionisation is achieved using a pneumatic nebuliser which turns the sample solution into a supersonic spray of small droplets. Ions are formed when the solvent evaporates and the statistically unbalanced charge distribution on the droplets leads to a net charge.

candidates.label: thermospray mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a pressurised solution of the sample is forced through a heated metal capillary tip. Ions are formed when the solvent evaporates and the statistically unbalanced charge distribution on the droplets leads to a net charge.

candidates.label: thermal ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where ionisation is achieved by loading the sample onto a heated filament.

candidates.label: particle beam mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a liquid sample passes through a desolvation chamber producing a beam of microscopic solid particles.

candidates.label: plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas, such as Ar, containing free electrons).

candidates.label: capacitively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Plasma mass spectrometry where the plasma has been generated by a potential difference between two electrodes, one of which is grounded and one of which is live.

candidates.label: electron cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Plasma mass spectrometry where the plasma has been generated by superimposing a static magnetic field and a high-frequency electromagnetic field at the electron cyclotron resonance frequency (the frequency at which an electron precesses in a magnetic field).

candidates.label: glow-discharge mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Plasma mass spectrometry where the plasma has been generated by passing an electrical discharge between two electrodes under reduced pressure. The ions are then characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Plasma mass spectrometry where the plasma has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: electrothermal vaporisation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Plasma mass spectrometry where the sample is vaporised by depositing it on a probe which is rapidly heated (to >1000 deg C) by passing a current through it.

candidates.label: slurry electrothermal vaporisation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: ETV-ICP-MS where the solid sample is prepared by grinding into a fine powder and suspension in a diluent such as 0.1% HNO3.

candidates.label: slurry nebulisation electrothermal vaporisation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a solid sample is ground to a fine powder and suspended in a diluent (such as 0.1% HNO3) before being vaporised by a probe which is rapidly heated by passing a current through it. The vaporised sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: solid sampling electrothermal vaporisation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a solid sample is vaporised by depositing it on a probe which is rapidly heated by passing a current through it. The vaporised sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: high performance liquid chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: high-performance liquid chromatography fluorescence detection-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography with fluorescence detection before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: high-performance liquid chromatography photodiode array-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography with photodiode array detection before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: high-resolution inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction. The 'exact' mass of the sample ions is then determined as opposed to the 'nominal' mass (the number of protons and neutrons).

candidates.label: inductively coupled plasma field sector mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction. The beam of ions is then directed into magnetic field, the orientation of which is perpendicular to the beam. The magnetic field forces the charged particles into different circular trajectories, the radii of which depend on the strength of the magnetic field, the accelerating voltage, and the mass of the ion.

candidates.label: inductively coupled plasma three dimensional quadrupole mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction. The mass-to-charge ratio of the sample ions is then measured whilst the ions are held in a stable orbit by an electric field generated by three electrodes.

candidates.label: inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction. The sample ions with different masses are then accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured.

candidates.label: laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is vaporised using a laser pulse then ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: laser ablation inductively coupled plasma time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is vaporised using a laser pulse then ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction. The sample ions with different masses are then accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: multiple collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction. A series of collectors ised used to detect several ion beams simultaneously.

candidates.label: size-exclusion chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by size-exclusion chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: size-exclusion chromatography-high-performance liquid chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by size-exclusion and high-performance liquid chromatographies before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: solution inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a sample mixture (a solution in dilute HNO3) is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: solution nebulisation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a sample mixture (a solution in dilute HNO3) is passed through a nebuliser to form a mist of finely dispersed droplets before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: microwave-induced plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by microwave radiation.

candidates.label: plasma desorption mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by bombarding the sample (mounted on a thin foil) with a highly energietic fission fragment from 252Cf.

candidates.label: secondary ion mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry in which the sample is bombarded with a stream of primary mass-selected particles and the secondary ions ejected from the sample are detected.

candidates.label: dynamic secondary ion mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A secondary ion mass spectrometry in which the sample is bombarded with a continuous focused beam of primary mass-selected ions which remove material from the surface of the sample by sputtering.

candidates.label: sputtered neutral atom mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is bombarded with a continuous focused beam of primary mass-selected ions which remove material from the surface of the sample by sputtering. The neutral atoms ejected from the sample are ionised and detected.

candidates.label: fast-atom bombardment mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A secondary ion mass spectrometry in which the sample (which is held in a liquid matrix) is bombarded with a stream of primary noble gas atoms.

candidates.label: mass spectrometry of recoiled ions
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is bombarded with a stream of primary mass-selected particles and the secondary elemental ions (usually H+, D+ or He+) ejected from the sample are detected.

candidates.label: time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is bombarded with a stream of primary mass-selected particles and the secondary ions ejected from the sample are detected by accelerating them to the same (known) kinetic energy and measuring the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: secondary electron emission mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a surface is bombarded with sample ions and the secondary electrons emitted are detected.

candidates.label: sector field mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample ions are directed into magnetic field, the orientation of which is perpendicular to the beam. The magnetic field forces the charged particles into different circular trajectories, the radii of which depend on the strength of the magnetic field, the accelerating voltage, and the mass of the ion.

candidates.label: selected ion flow tube mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by introducing it into a tube containing fast flowing He gas and ions such as H3O+, NO+ and O2+.

candidates.label: proton transfer reaction mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by introducing it into a tube containing fast flowing He gas and H3O+ ions.

candidates.label: spark source mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by a vacuum spark discharge, which is generated by a pulsed high (25–100 kV) potential difference between two electrodes.

candidates.label: tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry involving multiple mass-selection steps, with some form of fragmentation occurring between each stage.

candidates.label: collision-induced dissociation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry involving multiple mass-selection steps, where the sample ions are allowed to collide with neutral gas molecules (resulting in fragmentation) between each mass-selection stage.

candidates.label: electrospray ionisation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry involving multiple mass-selection steps, with some form of fragmentation occurring between each stage. Sample ionisation is achieved by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 uL min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets.

candidates.label: high-performance liquid chromatography-electrospray ionisation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where the sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography before being ionised by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of it through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 uL min1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets. The ions are then characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance by two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: tandem quadrupole mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry involving multiple mass-selection steps, with some form of fragmentation occurring between each stage. The mass-to-charge ratios of the sample ions are measured whilst the ions are held in a stable orbit by an electric field generated by four parallel electrodes.

candidates.label: time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry in which sample ions with different masses are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being ionised and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance using two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Any method where the sample is first separated by capillary electrophoresis, before being analysed by mass spectrometry.

candidates.label: capillary electrophoresis-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a sample mixture is first separated by capillary electrophoresis, before being ionised in a plasma which has been generated by electromagnetic induction and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: direct analysis in real time mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by a corona discharge within a He atmosphere.

candidates.label: electrospray ionisation Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 microlitre min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets. The mass-to-charge ratio of the ions is then determined by measuring their cyclotron frequency (the frequency at which they precesses in a fixed magnetic field) and subjecting it to a Fourier transform.

candidates.label: electrophoresis-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Any method where the sample is first separated by electrophoresis, before being analysed by mass spectrometry.

candidates.label: two-dimensional gel electrophoresis-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis, before being converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: direct analysis in real time time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by a corona discharge within a He atmosphere. Sample ions with different masses are then accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: ambient ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Any mass spectrometry technique where the sample is ionised at low or ambient temperature.

candidates.label: low-temperature plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) generated by an alternating current.

candidates.label: laser mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is illuminated with a laser.

candidates.label: ultra-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by ultra-performance liquid chromatography before being converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: high-performance liquid chromatography-nuclear magnetic resonance-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography before the energy states of spin-active nuclei in the sample, placed in a static magnetic field, are interrogated by inducing transitions between the states via radio frequency irradiation. The sample is then converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: extractive electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: An electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry in which a neutral sample, in the form of a gas or aerosol flow, is ionised by directing it into a plume of charged droplets, generated by forcing a solution of pure solvent through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1-10 microlitres per minute) into an electric field.

candidates.label: high resolution fast-atom bombardment mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (which is held in a liquid matrix) is bombarded with a stream of primary noble gas atoms and the secondary ions ejected from the sample are detected. The 'exact' mass of these secondary is then determined, as opposed to the 'nominal' mass (the number of protons and neutrons).

candidates.label: matrix-assisted laser desorption–ionisation quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser. The sample is held in a matrix (such as dihydrobenzoic acid) to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules. In the first stage the ions are held in a stable orbit by an electric field generated by four parallel electrodes (a quadrupole). In the second stage the sample ions are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: gas chromatography time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography then sample ions with different masses are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: electrospray ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets and where sample ions with different masses are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-electrospray ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being ionised by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets and where sample ions with different masses are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: reversed-phase liquid chromatography-electrospray ionisation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where the sample mixture is first separated by reverse-phase liquid chromatography before being ionised by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of it through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 uL min1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets. The ions are then characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance by two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: discharge mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by an electrical discharge.

candidates.label: dielectric barrier discharge ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by passing an alternating-voltage electrical discharge between a Cu sheet electrode and a discharge electrode separated by a glass slide. The glass slide acts as dielectric barrier and sample molecules on the surface of the glass slide are desorbed and ionised by the plasma.

candidates.label: capillary liquid chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by capillary liquid chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being ionised by forcing the solution (usually in an organic solvent) through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets.

candidates.label: nanoflow liquid chromatography-electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography (with a flow rate of nL min-1) before being ionised by forcing the solution (usually in an organic solvent) through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets. The ions are then characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-ion trap mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Amethod where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being ionised, and the mass-to-charge ratio of the sample ions is measured whilst the ions are held in a stable orbit by an electric or magnetic field.

candidates.label: nanoflow liquid chromatography chip enabled ion trap mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography (flow rate nL min-1) before being passed though a 'chip' (a microfluidic device) to the mass spectrometer where the mass-to-charge ratio of the sample ions is measured whilst the ions are held in a stable orbit by an electric or magnetic field.

candidates.label: atmospheric pressure glow discharge mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised under atmospheric pressure in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by passing an electrical discharge between two electrodes.

candidates.label: atmospheric pressure glow discharge tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised under atmospheric pressure in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by passing an electrical discharge between two electrodes. multiple mass-selection steps are used, with some form of fragmentation occurring between each stage.

candidates.label: high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography before being converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: orthogonal acceleration mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised and the ions are accelerated to very high kinetic energies by an ion source that works by sampling an ion beam travelling in a direction orthogonal to the axis of the flight path in the mass-to-charge analyser.

candidates.label: orthogonal acceleration time of flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised and the ions are accelerated to the same (known) very high kinetic energies by an ion source that works by sampling an ion beam travelling in a direction orthogonal to the axis of the flight path in the mass-to-charge analyser. The time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: mass spectrum
candidates.definition: A spectrum plotting relative abundance (%) vs. mass-to-charge ratio obtained from a mass spectrometry experiment.

candidates.label: thermospray mass spectrum
candidates.definition: A plot of relative abundance (%) vs. mass-to-charge ratio obtained from a mass spectrometry experiment where the ions are obtained by forcing a pressurised solution of the sample through a heated metal capillary tip.

candidates.label: thermogravimetry-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: The MS analysis of volatile compounds released during the measurement of the mass of a sample as a function of temperature.

candidates.label: sol–gel-assisted laser desorption-ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser. The sample is held in a sol–gel matrix to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules. The sample molecular ions are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: surface-enhanced laser desorption–ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser. The sample is mixed with a matrix compound (such as crystallised dihydrobenzoic acid) and deposited on a surface, with some chemical functionality, to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules. The sample molecular ions are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: dynamic reaction cell inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction. The sample is held in a dynamic reaction cell which contains a reagent gas that reacts preferentially with certain species, in order to allow only the analyte ions into the mass-to-charge analyser and the detector.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: ion-exchange chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by ion-exchange chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: plasma-assisted desorption–ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A plasma mass spectrometry in which a plasma is directed onto the surface of interest causing desorption of sample molecules from the surface and subsequent ionisation.

candidates.label: electrospray-assisted laser desorption-ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where neutral molecules are desorbed from the sample (usually biological) using a nitrogen laser and then ionised by collision with charged solvent droplets which are formed by forcing the solvent through a small heated capillary into an electric field.

candidates.label: dual-inlet isotope ratio mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where purified gas obtained from a sample is alternated rapidly with a standard gas (of known isotopic composition) by means of a system of valves, so that a number of comparative measurements are made of both gases. The relative abundance of isotopes in a sample is then determined.

candidates.label: continuous-flow isotope ratio mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the relative abundance of isotopes in a sample is determined. Measurements are taken immediately after sample preparation and separately to the standard gas.

candidates.label: gas chromatography
candidates.definition: A column chromatography "in which the mobile phase is a gas."

candidates.label: gas-solid chromatography
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography in which the stationary phase is a solid.

candidates.label: gas-liquid chromatography
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography "in which the stationary phase is a liquid."

candidates.label: magnetic sector mass spectrometer
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometer that uses a wedge-shaped magnetic field to separate the total ion beam into discrete ion beams according to the mass-to-charge ratio of the ions.

candidates.label: positive electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised to positive ions by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets.

candidates.label: positive electrospray ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised to positive ions by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets, and where sample ions with different masses are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: positive electrospray ionisation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry involving multiple mass-selection steps, with some form of fragmentation occurring between each stage. Sample ionisation is achieved by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 uL min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of positively charged droplets.

candidates.label: membrane-inlet mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry in which a thin membrane (usually made of a silicone elastomer) provides a selective means introducing low-molecular-weight volatile organic compounds into the ionisation source.

candidates.label: pyrolysis gas chromatography
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography in which chemical degradation of a sample by thermal energy takes place where the volatile pyrolysates are then separated by column chromatography.

candidates.label: pyrolysis gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first chemically degraded by heating then separated by gas chromatography then ionised and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-infrared spectroscopy
candidates.definition: Any method where a sample mixture is first separated by column chromatography where the mobile phase is a gas, then the absorption of radiation from the infrared region by the sample is measured.

candidates.label: pyrolysis gas chromatography-infrared spectroscopy
candidates.definition: Any method where a sample mixture is first chemically degraded by heating then separated by column chromatography where the mobile phase is a gas, then the absorption of radiation from the infrared region by the sample is measured.

candidates.label: pyrolysis mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry in which the sample is chemically degraded by thermal energy before being converted into gaseous ions.

candidates.label: desorption atmospheric pressure chemical ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where ionisation is achieved using a corona discharge which directs a liquid spray (composed of an inert, high velocity gas and solvent ions) onto the sample surface.

candidates.label: electrospray-ionisation quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Time-of-flight mass spectrometry where there is an initial electrospray ionisation stage.

candidates.label: electrospray-ionisation quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Tandem time-of-flight mass spectrometry where there is an initial electrospray ionisation stage.

candidates.label: reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: nanoflow high-performance liquid chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography (flow rate nL min-1) before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised by mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: nanoflow high-performance liquid chromatography-electrospray ionisation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where the sample mixture is first separated by high-performance liquid chromatography before being ionised by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of it through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of nL min1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets. The ions are then characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance by two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: reversed-phase nanoflow high-performance liquid chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry where the sample mixture is first separated by reversed-phase nanoflow high performance liquid chromatography.

candidates.label: nanoflow high-performance liquid chromatography electrospray-ionisation quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry where there is a nanoflow high-performance liquid chromatography separation step and an electrospray-ionisation mass selection step.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-flame ionisation detection
candidates.definition: Flame ionisation detection that is sensitive to compounds containing C-H bonds. The eluent is mixed with H2 and air and ignited. Any positively-charged radicals resulting from this process are collected at a cathode allowing the current to be measured.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-nitrogen-phosphorus detection
candidates.definition: Nitrogen-phosphorus detection where the input is from a gas chromatography separation.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-thermal energy analysis
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography method that is sensitive to compounds containing NO and NO2 groups. The eluent is pyrolysed (at 275 deg C) producing radicals, which react with ozone under low pressure to produce chemiluminescence.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-thermal conductivity detection
candidates.definition: Thermal conductivity detection where the sample is the eluent from a gas chromatography separation.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-flame photometric detection
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography method that is sensitive to sulfur- and phosphorus-containing compounds. The eluent is mixed with oxygen or air and ignited. Any chemiluminescence due to these compounds is then detected.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-pulsed discharge helium ionisation detection
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography method that is sensitive to small gas molecules (e.g. O2, N2, CO2). A low-power, pulsed DC discharge is used to ionise the eluent (which is held in He carrier gas). The resulting electrons are focused toward a collector electrode and the current is measured.

candidates.label: rotating-field mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry that uses sinusoidal radio frequency fields (in the x- and y- direction, differing in phase by 90°) during ion detection. The ions of a particular mass travel in a helix and impact an ion detector,  generating a pattern consisting of a set of concentric circles.

candidates.label: RapidFire(R) mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry, developed by BioTrove, which uses microfluidics to aspirate an aliquot of sample directly from a quenched assay plate and performs a solid-phase extraction on the sample before ionisation.

candidates.label: membrane extraction with a sorbent interface-gas chromatography
candidates.definition: A separation method where the sample is first transferred from one phase (the 'donor' or 'feed' phase) to another (the 'acceptor' or 'strip' phase) across a non-porous non-polar polymer membrane. The membrane extracts the analytes from their matrix, and these are subsequently trapped on a polymeric trap with a porous sorbent using a carrier gas stream. In the second step, the mixture in the carrier gas stream is further separated by gas chromatography.

candidates.label: low-temperature electrothermal vaporisation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a solid sample is vaporised by depositing it on a probe which is rapidly heated (to <1000 °C) by passing a current through it. The vaporised sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: nanoflow liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by nanoflow liquid chromatography (flow rate of nL min-1) before being converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance, by two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: two-dimensional liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated sequentially using two different liquid chromatography columns (commonly, ion-exchange followed by reversed-phase) before being analysed by two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: supercritical-fluid extraction-supercritical-fluid chromatography-gas chromatography
candidates.definition: An experimental method where the sample is first transferred to the liquid phase using a supercritical fluid, then subjected to column chromatography where the supercritical fluid acts as the mobile phase, and finally depressurised, collected and subjected to gas chromatography.

candidates.label: supercritical-fluid extraction-gas chromatography
candidates.definition: An experimental method where the sample is first transferred to the liquid phase using a supercritical fluid, then depressurised, collected and subjected to gas chromatography.

candidates.label: automated thermal desorption-gas chromatography mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first adsorbed onto packed tubes (e.g. Tenax) then each tube is automatically moved into a desorption oven and heated (100–280 °C for 5–20 min) to promote thermal desorption of the mixture into the headspace of the tube. The headspace is sampled and used for gas chromatography and the eluent is then ionised and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-pulse-discharge photoionisation detection
candidates.definition: A detection method where a DC voltage pulse is passed through a carrier gas generating high-energy (13.5–17.5 eV) photons which photoionise the elements a sample obtained by gas chromatography, and the current generated by this ionisation is measured.

candidates.label: atomic mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Spectrometry where the sample is atomised and converted into gaseous ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: molecular mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Spectrometry where the sample is converted into gaseous molecular ions, which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: strong-cation-exchange reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where the sample is first subjected to two-dimensional high-performance liquid chromatography (passed through two columns in sequence –-a primary ion-exchange column where the particles show no loss or gain of charge with varying pH, and a secondary column where the stationary phase is significantly less polar than the mobile phase). The eluent is then subjected to mass spectrometry where it is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: two-dimensional chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method in which a two-dimensional chromatography method is coupled to mass spectrometry.

candidates.label: tandem dual-column high-performance liquid chromatography inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where the sample is first subjected to column chromatography where the mobile phase is a liquid, the stationary phase consists of very small particles and the inlet pressure is relatively high. The sample passes through two columns (anion and cation exchange) in series. The eluent is then subjected to mass spectrometry where it is ionised in a plasma which has been generated by electromagnetic induction.

candidates.label: two-dimensional liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method in which a two-dimensional chromatography method , where the mobile phase is a liquid, is coupled to mass spectrometry,

candidates.label: two-dimensional high-performance liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method in which a two-dimensional chromatography method , where the mobile phase is a liquid and the inlet pressure is relatively high, is coupled to mass spectrometry,

candidates.label: strong-cation-exchange reversed-phase high-performance liquid chromatography atmospheric pressure chemical ionisation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where the sample is first subjected to two-dimensional high-performance liquid chromatography (passed through two columns in sequence –-a primary ion-exchange column where the particles show no loss or gain of charge with varying pH, and a secondary column where the stationary phase is significantly less polar than the mobile phase). The eluent is then subjected to mass spectrometry where it is ionised by interaction (electron or proton transfer) with reagent (N2, O2, H2O) gaseous ions at atmospheric pressure. The sample is analysed by two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: tandem dual-column high-performance liquid chromatography atmospheric pressure chemical ionisation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where the sample is first subjected to column chromatography where the mobile phase is a liquid, the stationary phase consists of very small particles and the inlet pressure is relatively high. The sample passes through two columns (anion and cation exchange) in series. The eluent is then subjected to mass spectrometry where it is ionised by interaction (electron or proton transfer) with reagent (N2, O2, H2O) gaseous ions at atmospheric pressure, and then analysed by two mass spectrometers in series.

candidates.label: electron transfer dissociation tandem mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry involving multiple mass-selection steps, where anions transfer electrons to multiply protonated peptides (resulting in fragmentation) between each mass-selection stage.

candidates.label: chiral stationary phase gas chromatography
candidates.definition: Column chromatography where the mobile phase is a gas and the stationary phase is a chiral, high-boiling-point, thermally-stable liquid such as a chiral polysiloxane.

candidates.label: ion-pair chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by ion-pair chromatography (where sample ions are 'paired' or neutralised and separated as an ion pair on a reversed-phase column) before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: partition chromatography
candidates.definition: A "chromatography in which separation is based mainly on differences between the solubility of the sample components in the stationary phase (gas chromatography), or on differences between the solubilities of the components in the mobile and stationary phases (liquid chromatography)"

candidates.label: liquid chromatography at the critical condition-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography, where the liquid is held at or near its critical point, before being converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography at the critical condition-electrospray ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography, where the liquid is held at or near its critical point, before being ionised by forcing the solution (usually in an organic solvent) through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets.

candidates.label: parallel ICP-MS and EI-MS detection after GC separation
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography before part of the sample is ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance. Another part of the sample is simultaneously ionised by electrons (energy 70 eV) which have been emitted from a glowing filament and accelerated through an electric field. The ions are then characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: low-temperature gas chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by low-temperature gas chromatography (-78°C) before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: high-resolution electrospray ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample is ionised by forcing a solution (usually in an organic solvent) of the sample through a small heated capillary (at a flow rate of 1–10 L min-1) into an electric field to produce a very fine mist of charged droplets, and where sample ions with different masses are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion and the 'exact' mass of the molecular ions in the sample is determined as opposed to the 'nominal' mass (the number of protons and neutrons).

candidates.label: gas chromatography electron ionisation mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography before being ionised by electrons (energy 70 eV) which have been emitted from a glowing filament and accelerated through an electric field. The ions are then characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: thermal desorption-gas chromatography mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first adsorbed onto packed tubes (e.g. Tenax) then moved into a desorption oven and heated (100–280 °C for 5–20 min) to promote thermal desorption of the mixture into the headspace of the tube. The headspace is sampled and used for gas chromatography and the eluent is then ionised and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: positive ion matrix-assisted laser desorption–ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the sample (usually a large organic molecule or biomolecule) is vaporised and ionised using a high-energy pulsed laser. The sample is held in a matrix (such as crystallised dihydrobenzoic acid) to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules. The positive sample ions are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: inverse gas chromatography
candidates.definition: A surface characterisation technique in which a pulse or constant concentration of a known gas or vapour (probe molecule) is injected into a column packed with the solid sample at a fixed carrier gas flow rate. The retention time of the probe molecule is then measured using a  traditional gas chromatography detector.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography-nuclear magnetic resonance-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before the energy states of spin-active nuclei in the sample, placed in a static magnetic field, are interrogated by inducing transitions between the states via radio frequency irradiation. The sample is then converted into ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry that uses a system with a quadrupole mass-to-charge analyser connected to a time-of-flight mass-to-charge analyser.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-microwave-induced plasma atomic emission detection
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography method that is sensitive to individual elements. The eluent is both atomised and excited by a microwave-induced plasma (a partially ionised gas containing free electrons and radicals). The characteristic radiation emitted by the atoms in the sample is then detected using a photodiode array.

candidates.label: paper spray mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Spectrometry where the sample spotted onto paper then solvent is applied and an electrically charged solvent is generated upon application of a high voltage. The ions are then characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: negative mode atmospheric pressure chemical ionization mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Atmospheric pressure chemical ionization mass spectrometry where the sample is ionized by interaction with negative ions.

candidates.label: positive mode atmospheric pressure chemical ionization mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Atmospheric pressure chemical ionization mass spectrometry where the sample is ionized by interaction with positive ions.

candidates.label: gas chromatography oven
candidates.definition: A piece of heating apparatus used to convert the sample into a gaseous mobile phase.

candidates.label: high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry
two-dimensional gas chromatography
candidates.definition: Chromatography where the mobile phase is a gas, initial separation proceeds in a primary column and parts of the eluent from this column are directed into a secondary column.

candidates.label: Fourier transform mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: An ion trap mass spectrometry in which the mass-to-charge ratio of the sample ions is determined by Fourier transform of a recorded time-domain transient.

candidates.label: Orbitrap mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Mass spectrometry where the mass-to-charge ratio of the sample ions is measured by their oscillations along the centre electrode in an Orbitrap mass analyzer.

candidates.label: preparative chromatography
candidates.definition: the use of a biomaterial's preferential affinity for either the mobile phase or the stationary phase to separate it from other materials of differing affinity

candidates.label: Mass spectrum
candidates.definition: Spectra from mass spectrometry.

candidates.label: Mass spectrometry data
candidates.definition: Data concerning a mass spectrometry measurement.

candidates.label: Mass spectrometry data format
candidates.definition: Format for mass pectra and derived data, include peptide sequences etc.

candidates.label: Gas chromatography mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Technique by which a mixture is separated into individual components by gas chromatography, followed by detection with a mass spectrometer. (Source: IUPAC; https://doi.org/10.1351/PAC-REC-06-04-06)

candidates.label: Mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Study of matter through the formation of gas-phase ions that are characterized using mass spectrometers by their mass, charge, structure, and/or physico-chemical properties. (Source: IUPAC; https://doi.org/10.1351/PAC-REC-06-04-06). Atomic mass spectrometric analysis involves: (1) atomization, (2) conversion of a substantial fraction of the atoms formed in step 1 to a stream of ions (usually singly charged positive ions), (3) separating the ions formed in step 2 on the basis of their mass-to-charge ratio (m/z), where m is the mass number of the ion and z is the number of fundamental charges that it bears, and (4) counting the number of ions of each type or measuring the ion current produced when the ions formed from the sample strike a suitable transducer.  (Skoog, Holler & Crouch, p. 253).  Molecular mass spectrometry is used to determine the structures of inorganic, organic, and biological molecules and the qualitative and quantitative composition of complex mixtures; The appearance of mass spectra for a given molecular species strongly depends on the method used for ion formation. That these methods fall into three major categories: gas-phase sources, desorption sources, and ambient desorption sources. (Skoog, Holler & Crouch, p. 502)

candidates.label: mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method for identifying molecules based on the detection of the mass-to-charge ratio of ions generated from the molecule by vaporisation and electron bombardment. Deflection of the ions through a magnetic field results in a characteristic pattern which is used to define the molecule of interest.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: An analytical technique in that combines the physical separation capabilities of gas chromatography (GC) with the mass analysis capabilities of mass spectrometry (MS). Molecular mixtures are initially vaporized and separated into components by GC. As these components exit the column, they are subjected to mass spectrometry for identification based on their mass-to-charge ratio and behavior in a magnetic field.

candidates.label: neutralization reionization mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: With this technique, m/z selected ions form neutrals by charge transfer to a collision gas or by dissociation. The neutrals are separated from the remaining ions and ionized in collisions with a second gas. This method is used to investigate reaction intermediates and other unstable species.

candidates.label: pyrolysis mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry technique in which the sample is heated to the point of decomposition and the gaseous decomposition products are introduced into the ion source.

candidates.label: mass spectrum
candidates.definition: A plot of the relative abundance of a beam or other collection of ions as a function of the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z).

candidates.label: MS1 spectrum

candidates.label: MSn spectrum
candidates.definition: MSn refers to multi-stage MS2 experiments designed to record product ion spectra where n is the number of product ion stages (progeny ions). For ion traps, sequential MS/MS experiments can be undertaken where n > 2 whereas for a simple triple quadrupole system n=2. Use the term ms level (MS:1000511) for specifying n.

candidates.label: mass spectrometry imaging
candidates.definition: A technique in which mass spectra are acquired in a spatially resolved manner. This is typically achieved by scanning a laser or primary ion beam over a sample and acquiring a mass spectrum at each position.

candidates.label: fast gas chromatography
candidates.definition: Fast gas chromatography (fast GC, FGC) employs short, narrow-bore capillary columns, high carrier gas velocity, and rapid temperature programming to achieve high-efficiency separations in a fraction of standard GC run times.

candidates.label: packed column gas chromatography
candidates.definition: Packed column gas chromatography uses stainless steel or glass tubes (typically 2–4 mm ID, 1–6 m length) filled with particulate packing material coated with stationary phase, enabling the separation of larger sample volumes but typically providing lower efficiency and broader peaks than capillary GC.

candidates.label: capillary column gas chromatography
candidates.definition: Capillary column gas chromatography uses narrow-bore fused silica columns (typically 0.1–0.5 mm ID, 5–100 m length) coated with a thin internal stationary phase, enabling high-efficiency, high-resolution separations of volatile analytes.

candidates.label: high-resolution gas chromatography
candidates.definition: High-resolution gas chromatography (HRGC) utilizes narrow-bore capillary columns and optimized parameters to achieve exceptional separation efficiency and peak capacity for complex, volatile mixtures.

candidates.label: pyrolysis-gas chromatography
candidates.definition: Pyrolysis-gas chromatography (Py-GC) thermally decomposes complex samples into smaller volatile fragments, which are separated using GC.

candidates.label: gas chromatography system
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography (GC) system comprises an injector, temperature-controlled column with stationary phase, carrier gas supply, oven, and detector, enabling separation of volatile analytes.

candidates.label: two-dimensional gas chromatography system
candidates.definition: A two-dimensional gas chromatography system (GC×GC) uses orthogonal column sets connected by a modulator, providing enhanced separation of complex mixtures via sequential, independent mechanisms in primary and secondary columns.

candidates.definition: A gas chromatography mass spectrometry system (GC–MS) integrates a gas chromatograph for volatile analyte separation with a mass spectrometer for ionization and detection, enabling sensitive qualitative or quantitative analysis.

candidates.definition: Comprehensive two-dimensional gas chromatography (GCxGC) is a multidimensional separation technique that utilizes two columns with different stationary phases connected by a modulator, which traps, focuses and reinjects fractions from the first column to the second. This approach leads to a 2D chromatogram offering higher peak capacity and separation power.

candidates.label: mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: Spectrometry where the sample is converted into gaseous ions which are characterised by their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-mass spectrometry

candidates.label: Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrometry
candidates.definition: An analytical technique wherein gas chromatography is coupled to mass spectrometry in order to separate, identify, and quantify substances in a sample.

candidates.label: liquid chromatography mass spectrometry platform
candidates.definition: A liquid chromatography mass spectrometry platform is a platform that is the collection of instrument, software and reagents needed to perform a liquid chromatography mass spectrometry protocol. definition_source: OBI.

candidates.label: mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: An assay that identifies the amount and type of material entities present in a sample by fragmenting the sample and measuring the mass-to-charge ratio of the resulting particles.

candidates.label: gas chromatography equipment
candidates.definition: Any device used in a gas chromatography experiment.

candidates.label: gas chromatography oven
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography oven is an oven with a heated connection between the GC and the MS instrument in a GCMS-analysis, that keeps compounds in the gas phase as they leave the GC oven.

candidates.label: gas chromatography detector
candidates.definition: A gas chromatography detector is a chromatography detector that locates in the dimensions of space and time, the positions of the components of a mixture that has been subjected to a gas chromatographic process and thus permits the senses to appreciate the nature of the separation. There is no LC detector that has an equivalent performance to the flame ionization detector (FID) used in GC. In general, LC detectors have sensitivities of two to three orders of magnitude less than their GC counterparts and linear dynamic ranges one to two orders of magnitude lower. Only highly specific LC detectors have sensitivities that can approach those of GC detectors.

candidates.label: mass spectrometry assay measuring MHC ligand processing and presentation of MHC ligands eluted from cellular MHC

candidates.label: mass spectrometry assay measuring MHC ligand processing and presentation of MHC ligands eluted from secreted MHC

candidates.label: mass spectrometry assay measuring binding of a B cell epitope:antibody complex

candidates.label: protein sequencing by tandem mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: A sequencing assay that detremines amino acid sequences of proteins using multiple rounds of mass spectrometry and molecule fragmentation.

candidates.label: mass spectrometry-based protein state assay
candidates.definition: A type of protein state assay that employs mass spectrometry to measure levels of proteins in different phosphorylation states.

candidates.label: targeted, drug-modulated, mass spectrometry-based protein phoshporylation-state assay
candidates.definition: A type of mass spectrometry protein state assay that measures levels of a targeted set of proteins in different phosphorylation states in response to drug perturbations.

candidates.label: tandem mass tag mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: A type of tandem mass spectrometry where isotopomer labels are employed for accurate quantification and identification of specific proteins.

candidates.label: global chromatin profiling by mass spectrometry assay

candidates.label: liquid chromatography mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry assay where a sample mixture is first separated by liquid chromatography before being converted into ions which are characterized by using mass spectrometry based on their mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.

candidates.label: matrix assisted laser desorption ionization imaging mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry assay that involves collection of spatially resolved mass spectra of a sample during microscopy where a pulse laser is used to produce both ionisation and vaporization. The sample is held in a matrix (such as dihydrobenzoic acid) to protect it from direct laser illumination and to separate the sample molecules. The spectra are used to visualise the spatial distribution of biomolecules by their molecular masses.

candidates.label: gas chromatography mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry assay combining mass spectrometry and gas chromatography for the qualitative as well as quantitative determination of compounds.

candidates.label: tandem mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry assay that uses two or more analyzers separated by a region in which ions can be induced to fragment by transfer of energy (frequently by collision with other molecules).

candidates.label: capillary electrophoresis mass spectrometry assay
candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry assay where a sample mixture is first separated by capillary electrophoresis before being analysed by mass spectrometry.

candidates.label: proteomics by mass spectrometry assay

candidates.label: metabolomics by mass spectrometry assay

candidates.label: Chromatographic process
candidates.definition: A chemical process by which mixtures of chemical entities are separated by their different partition coefficients between a stationary phase and a liquid phase

candidates.label: brominated poly[d(GC)].poly[d(GC)]
candidates.definition: A double-stranded DNA polynucleotide consisting of two complementary strands consisting of repeating units of brominated guanosine and deoxycytidine residues, all residues in each strand being connected by 3'→5' phosphodiester linkages. The sites of bromination are at C-8 of guanine and C-5 of cytosine, although not all these sites are brominated, with bromination at the guanine C-8 predominating.

candidates.label: brominated poly[d(GC)]

The sites of bromination are at C-8 of guanine and C-5 of cytosine, although not all these sites are brominated, with bromination at the guanine C-8 predominating.

candidates.definition: A mass spectrometry in which a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-isotope ratio mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography before being characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance of isotopes.

candidates.label: gas chromatography time-of-flight mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography then sample ions with different masses are accelerated to the same (known) kinetic energy and the time taken for each ion to reach a detector at a known distance is measured. This time is dependent on the mass-to-charge ratio of the ion.

candidates.label: gas chromatography-inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry
candidates.definition: A method where a sample mixture is first separated by gas chromatography before being ionised in a plasma (a partially ionised gas–-such as Ar–-containing free electrons) which has been generated by electromagnetic induction, and characterised according to mass-to-charge ratio and relative abundance.
